smell: Package `packages` wraps `platform.PackageManager.Install`/`Remove` with an extra logger.Info() envelope and a single `fmt.Errorf` rewrap. Three call sites consume it (setup/steps.go:305, cleanup/packages.go:67, cleanup/services.go:41). The value added is two log lines that could be written inline. 42 LOC total.
fix_summary: Inline the two functions at their call sites (setup/steps.go:305, cleanup/packages.go:67, cleanup/services.go:41) and delete internal/distribution/okd/packages. The logger.Info lines are already repeated in the callers' surrounding context. Alternatively, promote Install/Remove to methods on platform.Manager that handle the log envelope — one call site, one package.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: canonical helpers list (packages not listed)
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: addon.IsRegistered has no callers. However it is a clean symmetric API pair with Register/Get/All/Names/Enabled (if Register exists, IsRegistered stays by symmetric-API rubric). Flag as scaffolding rather than dead code.
fix_summary: Keep. addon.Register / Get / All / Names / Enabled form the matrix; IsRegistered is the obvious membership test. Verify against roadmap.md when touching the addon CLI; if a caller lands, move this from suggestion to not-a-finding.

smell: Manager.IsInstalled uses a bespoke `queryMatch` string substring to distinguish "installed" from "purged" on dpkg output. The logic is correct but the two-branch design (empty → exit-code-only, non-empty → substring match) is a mini-DSL inside a single method. Splitting into two tiny methods (isInstalledRHEL/isInstalledDebian) or delegating to a per-family func field would read more plainly.
fix_summary: Replace the `queryMatch` string field with `postCheck func(stdout []byte, pkg string) bool` on Manager. Set it to a no-op in the RHEL constructor and a dpkg-ii-prefix check in the Debian constructor. Method body becomes `return m.postCheck(output, pkg), nil`.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: getDiskSizes returns `(cpDisk, workerDisk, workerDataDisk, masterDataDisk int)` — four unnamed integers with no semantic ordering. The named returns document the positional identity, but the real signal a caller needs is 'which is which'. A struct (or four explicit calls) would be safer; the current shape is a 4-int tuple begging for a mis-reordering bug.
fix_summary: Replace the 4-int tuple with a `type diskSizes struct { cpOS, workerOS, workerData, masterData int }` and return the struct. The single caller (buildTerraformVarsData) then assigns by field name, not by position.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: OKDVersion.Major() and OKDVersion.Minor() parse the Version string via fmt.Sscanf on every call. ShortVersion calls both (two parses per call), and callers invoke the methods inside filter loops (fetcher.go parseReleases and sortAndClassifySeries, cli/releases.go), so a list of ~40 releases runs dozens of Sscanf parses per display even though the version string is immutable per OKDVersion.
fix_summary: Parse once at unmarshal time (or memoize). Either (a) add unexported `major, minor int` fields and populate them in the fetcher's parseVersionTag flow (fetcher.go:241 already runs Sscanf — fold the result into the struct), or (b) use `strings.Cut(v.Version, ".")` + strconv.Atoi, which is faster and avoids the fmt machinery.
rule_source: Uber §Avoid String Concatenation in Loops (analogue: avoid fmt in loops)

smell: buildISOStrings and buildNodeNames in setup/terraform.go are structurally identical: allocate []string of length count, loop `for i := range count`, format `"%s:iso/%s%d.iso"` vs `"%s-%s%d"`. Both take (isoStorage/clusterName, phase.NodeRole, count). A single helper parameterized on the format string — or a tabular/template-driven approach — would de-duplicate. Low value today, but a new role (e.g. bastion-managed VM) doubles the edit.
fix_summary: Introduce `buildQuotedRoleList(format string, prefix string, role phase.NodeRole, count int) []string` that takes a format string with two %s + one %d and renders count elements. Both sites collapse to one-liners. Alternatively, accept the duplication as 'readable over clever' — the two names tell the reader more than a single generic helper would.
rule_source: Go proverb: A little copying is better than a little dependency (counter-argument to refactor — so this is a judgment call)

smell: mergeNamedList has four nested type-assertion chains to walk a generic YAML tree (any → []any → map[string]any → map[string]any['name'] → string). Function works and the any is load-bearing (YAML unmarshal targets `any` for open schemas), but the walk is tightly coupled to one semantic (merge-by-name) so the any-ness doesn't buy reuse. A typed named-entry helper or kubeconfig-specific types would read more plainly.
fix_summary: Either (a) declare a minimal kubeconfig schema (ClustersList, UsersList, ContextsList) and yaml-unmarshal into typed slices, then merge; or (b) extract a `namedEntries(v any) map[string]any` helper so the tree walk lives in one place. (a) is the clean fix but adds types the package doesn't need elsewhere; (b) preserves the any-based approach but shrinks the walk to one site.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: distribution.StepBuilder.Build() has no external callers; every production path goes through BuildSteps → MustBuild, and MustBuild is Build's only caller. Build's stated value is 'returns an error only when b is nil' but NewStepBuilder is the only way to get a *StepBuilder and it never returns nil, so the error is unreachable. Either Build is scaffolding (symmetric Build/MustBuild pair) or it could be inlined into MustBuild.
fix_summary: Keep. Build/MustBuild is the canonical pair for fluent builders in Go (errors.New + errors.Must, template.New + template.Must, etc.), and CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes names StepDef + BuildSteps as canonical. If the nil-guard error is ever removed, inline Build into MustBuild and drop the symmetric pair.
